study: Honest early entry: is there a rule, knowable at the minute it fires, that buys names on the live board before the surge the desk currently buys late, and beats a random later minute of the same name (and, as information, a same-minute other board name)?
registered_at: 2026-10-13, before any script run and before any return from these rules was computed
origin: 2026-10-13 AGY ran tools/studies/early_entry_sim.py: the desk's own fills bought 5 minutes earlier turn -$121 into +$174 over 531 October trades (t 4.38), rising to +$420 at 10 minutes. That shift is look-ahead: the desk bought at M because the tape had already risen, so buying at M-5 assumes knowing at M-5 that the signal was coming. Profit that keeps rising the longer the lead is the tell. The claim used to justify the pre-square arm (6bae9f8), premarket seating (577d3cb) and the 09:45 start (689dfca) is that pre-square fires 3-5 minutes before the full square and so catches the surge. This prereg tests that with rules that only read bars that had already closed.
prior: Square and pre-square arms matched random minutes on runway (square-arms-show-no-runway, 9/29; sr-levels note 10/6: squares ~0 gross vs honest controls). %R crosses and both-rising matched random minutes (wr_trigger_study). Volume breakout was +9 bp on SIP and ~0 on IEX. The prior is FAIL.

rules.series: signals.compute_percent_r_exhaustion on IEX 1-minute bars (the live feed), extended hours from 04:00 ET for warm-up, cfg = latch_gate_sim.CFG (fast %R(21) EMA 7, slow %R(112) EMA 3). The frame is minute-gridded first exactly as signals._minute_grid_pr does (gaps of 2..MINUTE_GAP_FILL_MAX=15 minutes filled with flat bars at the previous close, volume 0), so row i-1 is minute m-1. Rising = the smoothed line above the previous minute's value by more than rte_direction_eps 0.05, as live _live_percent_r_line (ai_entry_watch.py:11155).
rules.PRE: Bar-close approximation of the live empty square (_presquare_exh_allows_buy): fast >= -35 and slow >= -35, |fast - slow| <= 15, NOT (fast >= -20 and slow >= -20), fast rising. Onset on the completed bar. Differences from live, stated: live evaluates inside the bar against the live price and so can fire up to ~1 minute earlier; live needs ai_watch_square_min_count=2 consecutive polls, which are seconds apart and have no bar-level meaning; live's 'cooling' refusal is pctr_falling, already excluded by requiring rising.
rules.IGN: Ignition, the explicit 'earlier' candidate, fixed here and not tuned. On the IEX bar of minute m: close[m] / close at-or-before minute m-3 - 1 >= 0.0025 AND volume[m] >= 2.0 x the mean IEX volume over the 20 RTH minutes m-20..m-1, where a minute with no IEX bar counts as volume 0 (no IEX trades) and the mean must be > 0. Premarket minutes never enter the mean. Fires on onset (flag false on the previous IEX bar).
rules.SQ: Full square, information only: fast >= -20 and slow >= -20, |fast - slow| <= 15, fast rising (same definition of rising). Onset. Cannot pass or fail the study.
rules.refractory: After an on-board fire, the same rule does not fire again on the same name for 15 minutes. An onset off the board is counted and does not start the refractory.
rules.window: Signal bar start from 09:50 through 15:30 ET inclusive (09:50 so IGN has 20 RTH bars; the same window for every rule).
rules.on_board: The signal minute must be a board minute: at least one ai_reports/decision_ledger row with stage 'watch' or 'arm' for that symbol whose ts falls in that ET minute. A fire off the board is not counted and is not scored.

fill_and_markout: Entry at the SIP open of the bar starting one minute after the signal bar. Primary exit: SIP close of the bar starting 9 minutes after the entry bar (10-minute hold). The exit bar must start before 16:00, for rules and controls at every hold. A missing entry or exit bar drops the signal (counted). Timing test, not a book replay.
cost: 10 bp round trip, fixed, subtracted from rule and control alike. It cancels in the lift and remains in the net. Gross is printed too.
control: For each scored signal, one random later entry minute of the same name and session: uniformly from entry+1 .. entry+60 minutes, whose entry bar and 10-minute exit bar both exist and whose exit bar starts before 16:00. Held identically. Board membership is NOT required for the control (staying on the board depends on the path). Seed sha256(symbol|day|entry_minute|rule|early-honest-v1). No eligible minute: the signal is dropped and counted. Why later only: a same-hour control can sit on the run-up that made a momentum rule fire. On a driftless synthetic walk (30 days x 15 names), same-hour controls scored PRE -12, IGN -7, SQ -21 bp with |t| 2.3-7.3; later-only controls scored all three within +/-3.5 bp, |t| < 1.4. A residual bias of the later control is the post-fire drift over <= 60 minutes; it is rule-dependent, and bounded by the cross-sectional control (information) and the net > 0 bar.
statistic: lift = (rule net) - (control net) per signal. Day-equal mean (mean of per-day means) and day-clustered t. Days with no scored signal are absent.
data: Every ET session date that has an ai_reports/decision_ledger/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl with board rows, on the mini. Bars fetched for every board symbol of that day, IEX and SIP, 04:00-16:05 ET. Fetch misses (including Alpaca 429s) are counted per day; a day with > 5% of board names missing on either feed is excluded and listed. The day list and the split are printed before any return. A day excluded for misses is deleted from the fetch skip-list and refetched on the next --fetch. Inventory mode prints per day: board size, IEX and SIP miss %, and onset counts before the board filter (no returns).
split: Sorted usable days; the median index (n-1)//2 is the last day of half A, later days are half B.
pass: Scored separately for PRE and IGN. Each half is PASS (day-equal lift >= +5 bp, day-clustered t >= 2.0, day-equal net > 0, >= 100 scored signals, >= 6 days with a scored signal), UNDERPOWERED (short of signals or days), or FAIL. A rule is PASS only if both halves PASS; FAIL if either half FAILs; otherwise UNDERPOWERED. UNDERPOWERED is not a pass and is not evidence against the rule. Two rules graded; a single-rule pass is reported with that multiplicity stated. Signals per half are printed before the table.
information_only: gross means; 5, 15 and 30 minute markouts with the same control

lead: for each desk fill (outcomes.jsonl, entry_path 'watch', scored days) the minutes from the latest PRE / IGN / SQ fire on that name in the prior 15 minutes to the fill; median and share >= 3 min. This tests the claim that pre-square fires 3-5 minutes earlier
hit rate: share of PRE and IGN fires followed by a desk fill on the same name within 10 minutes

artifact demo: for random board minutes t whose SIP close rose >= 14 bp over the prior 5 minutes, AGY's shift lift (buy at open of t-5 vs open of t+1, both sold at the 10-minute exit). Shows the shift method's gain on minutes with no rule at all
drop counts: off-board, no entry/exit bar, no control, fetch miss, excluded days
cross-sectional control: lift vs a random other board name at the same signal minute, same entry and hold
every board minute in the window, gross 10-minute markout (the unconditional base rate)
share of later controls whose entry falls inside the rule's 10-minute hold
entry at the SIP close of the entry bar instead of its open (the IEX signal bar is surely published), same control
no_retuning: Thresholds -35/-20/15, lookback 2, IGN 0.25% over 3 bars and 2.0x volume over 20 bars, 15-minute refractory, 10-minute hold, 10 bp cost and the window are fixed. Any other value is a new prereg.
if_pass: A pass earns a result-skeptic review of the positive. It does not change bot_config or the live arms.
if_fail: A FAIL (not UNDERPOWERED) on PRE and IGN retires the shift sweep as evidence that an earlier rule exists. It says nothing about the live arm's intra-bar timing beyond the ~1 minute stated in rules.PRE; the pre-square arm, premarket seating and 09:45 start are then judged on their own measured fills.
script: tools/studies/early_entry_honest.py. --fetch builds caches (mini only). The default prints the data inventory and split, no returns. --score must not be run until this file has a result-skeptic READY. Rule flags, onset, refractory, control choice and markout are covered by tests/test_early_entry_honest.py, which reads no market data.
calibration: tests/test_early_entry_honest.py::test_control_is_unbiased_after_a_selected_rise, plus the synthetic null run above. On that null the artifact demo (AGY's shift-5 method on rule-free rising minutes) scored +44.5 bp, t 53.
amended: 2026-10-13, before any score on market data: control changed from same-hour to later-minute after the null calibration; IGN wording made exact (missing IEX minutes are 0 volume; reference close is at or before m-3). Round 2 after result-skeptic FIX FIRST, still before any score: live minute-grid + eps rising, PRE named a bar-close approximation with differences stated, UNDERPOWERED distinct from FAIL, exit before 16:00, refractory wording, refetch of excluded days, inventory per day, five information lines (cross control, base rate, overlap share, close entry, 20 bp). Round 2 READY; wording fixed after it (study line, control drift sentence, docstring, count). Fetch drops symbols Alpaca rejects as invalid (ledger test junk such as SMOKE1) and retries the chunk; dropped symbols count as misses.
rescore_warm_2026_10_15: Corrected re-run, not a new hypothesis: the 10/13 scoring computed the slow %R line (112 bars) on same-day bars only, so it did not exist before ~11:20 and the morning was effectively unscored (found by the result-skeptic on os_leave_prereg.json, 2026-10-15). Re-scored with --warm (both lines warmed on the prior sessions' IEX bars, as live loads 5 days; days > 5% without prior bars excluded and listed). Same rules, controls, costs, split and pass bar. The original cold-start result files are kept; the warm result is written beside them (_warm). Registered before the warm re-score ran.
